sentences.en: This is 99% Invisible.
sentences.zh: 这里是《99%隐形》。

sentences.en: I'm Roman Mars.
sentences.zh: 我是罗曼·马尔斯。

sentences.en: When I look at a body of water, I assume that it's teeming with microbes.
sentences.zh: 每当我看到一片水域，我就会想里面肯定挤满了微生物。

sentences.en: And for that reason, I wouldn't fill my water bottle from a puddle or a pond or probably even a stream
sentences.zh: 正因如此，我绝不会从水坑、池塘，甚至可能连溪流里往水瓶里灌水，

sentences.en: because I know that I have a chance of getting a waterborne disease.
sentences.zh: 因为我知道自己有感染水源性疾病的风险。

sentences.en: But I don't apply the same scrutiny to the air I breathe,
sentences.zh: 但我却不会用同样的眼光去审视我呼吸的空气，

sentences.en: which is a little odd because it too is chock full of life.
sentences.zh: 这有点奇怪，因为空气中也充满了生命。

sentences.en: Scientists call it the aerobiome.
sentences.zh: 科学家称之为“空气生物群落”。

sentences.en: It's this huge ecosystem that we really barely understand at all.
sentences.zh: 这是一个我们几乎完全不了解的巨大生态系统。

sentences.en: This is science writer Carl Zimmer, who has written an amazing new book called Airborne,
sentences.zh: 这位是科普作家卡尔·齐默，他写了一本令人惊叹的新书，书名叫《空气传播》，

sentences.en: all about the life that is wafting about in the air all around us.
sentences.zh: 书中讲述了我们周围空气中漂浮着的各种生命。

sentences.en: The aerobiome is not just important for how nature itself works,
sentences.zh: 空气生物群落不仅对自然界的运作至关重要，

sentences.en: but you are breathing in living things pretty much with every breath.
sentences.zh: 而且你每一次呼吸，几乎都在吸入活着的生物。

sentences.en: You know, most of the time they don't kill you.
sentences.zh: 你知道，大多数时候它们不会要了你的命。

sentences.en: But, you know, when you have a pandemic, sometimes a lot of people do die.
sentences.zh: 但是，你也知道，当大流行病来袭时，有时确实会有很多人死亡。

sentences.en: Carl Zimmer's book is a scientific history of the air and its relationship to disease.
sentences.zh: 卡尔·齐默的书是一部关于空气及其与疾病关系的科学史。

sentences.en: I started reading the book for fun, but I decided to interview Carl on the show
sentences.zh: 我起初读这本书只是为了消遣，但我决定在节目中采访卡尔，

sentences.en: because it actually has a lot to do with architecture.
sentences.zh: 因为这实际上与建筑学有很大关系。

sentences.en: Most of our breathing happens indoors,
sentences.zh: 我们大部分时间都在室内呼吸，

sentences.en: and yet modern architects rarely design buildings with airborne disease in mind.
sentences.zh: 然而现代建筑师在设计建筑时，很少考虑到空气传播的疾病。

sentences.en: Carl Zimmer thinks that's in part because for over a century,
sentences.zh: 卡尔·齐默认为，这在一定程度上是因为一个多世纪以来，

sentences.en: scientific institutions have been reluctant to take the air seriously as an important vector for disease.
sentences.zh: 科学机构一直不愿将空气视为一种重要的疾病传播媒介。

sentences.en: We got a taste of this during the early days of the COVID-19 pandemic,
sentences.zh: 在新冠疫情初期，我们对此深有体会，

sentences.en: when there was a lot of conflict and confusion about whether the virus was airborne
sentences.zh: 当时关于病毒是否通过空气传播，

sentences.en: and what airborne even means.
sentences.zh: 以及“空气传播”到底意味着什么，存在着大量的冲突和困惑。

sentences.en: But this conflict and confusion, it didn't start in 2020.
sentences.zh: 但这种冲突和困惑并非始于2020年。

sentences.en: I mean, the fact is that our struggle to understand the air
sentences.zh: 我的意思是，事实上，我们对于空气的理解，

sentences.en: and what the air means to us and our health actually goes back thousands of years.
sentences.zh: 以及空气对我们和我们健康意味着什么的探索，其实可以追溯到几千年前。

sentences.en: So, okay, so I want you to guide us through this history of how we think about the air
sentences.zh: 那么，我想请你带我们梳理一下这段历史，看看我们是如何看待空气

sentences.en: and its relationship to disease.
sentences.zh: 及其与疾病的关系的。

sentences.en: So where should we start?
sentences.zh: 我们应该从哪里开始呢？

sentences.en: Well, if you go way back to the ancient world,
sentences.zh: 嗯，如果你回溯到古代世界，

sentences.en: there were a lot of concepts about the air being the cause of many diseases.
sentences.zh: 当时有很多关于空气是许多疾病之源的观念。

sentences.en: And so Hippocrates would talk about miasmas,
sentences.zh: 希波克拉底会谈到“瘴气”，

sentences.en: which were like a corruption of the air.
sentences.zh: 这就像是一种空气的腐败。

sentences.en: You know, why is it that all these people in this village all got the plague around the same time?
sentences.zh: 你知道，为什么这个村庄里的所有人几乎在同一时间都得了瘟疫？

sentences.en: Well, it must be because there was a miasma in the air
sentences.zh: 嗯，那一定是因为空气中存在某种瘴气，

sentences.en: that just traveled along and everybody inhaled it and they all died.
sentences.zh: 它随风飘荡，每个人都吸入了它，然后他们就都死了。

sentences.en: So there was this powerful concept which held on in one way or another for many, many centuries.
sentences.zh: 所以，这个强有力的概念以这样或那样的方式存在了许多个世纪。

sentences.en: Could you describe what was the conception of what a miasma was?
sentences.zh: 你能描述一下当时人们对瘴气的概念吗？

sentences.en: Like, what was it made of?
sentences.zh: 比如，它是由什么构成的？

sentences.en: Like, I don't quite get it.
sentences.zh: 我不太明白。

sentences.en: Of course you don't get it because you don't live in ancient Greece
sentences.zh: 你当然不明白，因为你不是生活在古希腊，

sentences.en: and you don't have an ancient Greek worldview, you know?
sentences.zh: 你也没有古希腊人的世界观，对吧？

sentences.en: I mean, you got to think about the world as being made of four elements.
sentences.zh: 我的意思是，你得把世界看作是由四种元素构成的。

sentences.en: So you have to think about your body as being made of four humors.
sentences.zh: 所以你得把你的身体看作是由四种体液构成的。

sentences.en: I mean, it takes a lot of rejiggering to really try to even begin to understand
sentences.zh: 我的意思是，要真正开始理解希波克拉底在谈论什么，

sentences.en: what Hippocrates is talking about.
sentences.zh: 需要进行大量的思维重构。

sentences.en: It's a corruption.
sentences.zh: 这是一种腐败。

sentences.en: Corruption was a very powerful idea in ancient Western thought in particular.
sentences.zh: “腐败”在古代西方思想中是一个非常强大的概念。

sentences.en: And so, you know, you would have the four humors in your body,
sentences.zh: 所以，你知道，你的体内有四种体液，

sentences.en: which were in this delicate balance.
sentences.zh: 它们处于一种微妙的平衡之中。

sentences.en: And, you know, if you inhale this corrupted air, that would throw your humors out of balance.
sentences.zh: 而且，你知道，如果你吸入了这种腐败的空气，就会打破你体液的平衡。

sentences.en: I should add, like, miasmas were believed to be caused by lots of different things.
sentences.zh: 我应该补充一点，人们认为瘴气是由许多不同的事物引起的。

sentences.en: So they might be caused by bad weather.
sentences.zh: 它们可能是由恶劣的天气引起的。

sentences.en: They might be caused by the stars.
sentences.zh: 它们可能是由星象引起的。

sentences.en: They might be caused by waste lying on the ground or stagnant water.
sentences.zh: 它们可能是由地面上的废弃物或死水引起的。

sentences.en: So there were all these potential sources for corrupting the air.
sentences.zh: 所以，空气腐败有各种潜在的来源。

sentences.en: And then when you breathed it in, then you would get sick.
sentences.zh: 当你吸入它时，你就会生病。

sentences.en: And there were different miasmas for different diseases.
sentences.zh: 不同的疾病有不同的瘴气。

sentences.en: You know, plague, influenza, so on and on and on.
sentences.zh: 你知道，瘟疫、流感等等，不一而足。

sentences.en: Each one had its own miasma.
sentences.zh: 每种疾病都有其对应的瘴气。

sentences.en: So how did thinking about disease as a miasma affect the way people behaved?
sentences.zh: 那么，将疾病视为瘴气是如何影响人们的行为的？

sentences.en: Miasma would actually affect the way people built their world.
sentences.zh: 瘴气理论实际上影响了人们构建世界的方式。

sentences.en: The way that cities were designed and the way that houses were built.
sentences.zh: 影响了城市的设计方式和房屋的建造方式。

sentences.en: So canals would be built, you know, so that you didn't have water just getting stagnant.
sentences.zh: 所以人们会修建运河，你知道，这样水就不会停滞不前。

sentences.en: Waste would be required to be cleared out of the center of cities.
sentences.zh: 城市中心会被要求清理废弃物。

sentences.en: When you had reform movements in Britain in the 1700s
sentences.zh: 当18世纪英国出现改革运动时，

sentences.en: that were trying to improve the health of people in prisons,
sentences.zh: 他们试图改善监狱中人们的健康状况，

sentences.en: people were dying in prisons of diseases, including something they would call jail fever.
sentences.zh: 当时人们死于监狱中的各种疾病，包括一种他们称之为“监狱热”的病。

sentences.en: They thought what you needed to do was to bring in fresh air.
sentences.zh: 他们认为你需要做的是引入新鲜空气。

sentences.en: Because wholesome, fresh air would replace the stagnant air that, you know,
sentences.zh: 因为健康、新鲜的空气会取代那些积聚在监狱里、

sentences.en: filled with miasmas that was building up inside these prisons.
sentences.zh: 充满瘴气的停滞空气。

sentences.en: And so there was even a British prison that had a windmill built on the roof
sentences.zh: 甚至有一座英国监狱在屋顶上建了一座风车，

sentences.en: to try to circulate fresh air through the whole building.
sentences.zh: 试图让新鲜空气在整栋建筑中循环。

sentences.en: And so a lot of the response to this belief in miasmas was urban planning and architecture.
sentences.zh: 所以，对这种瘴气信仰的许多回应都体现在城市规划和建筑上。

sentences.en: I want to bring in this character, or this person that is a character in your book
sentences.zh: 我想引出这个人物，或者说你书中的这个角色，

sentences.en: named Max von Pettenkoffer.
sentences.zh: 名叫马克斯·冯·佩滕科弗。

sentences.en: Can you tell me about him and where he sits in the miasma world?
sentences.zh: 你能跟我讲讲他吗？他在瘴气世界里处于什么位置？

sentences.en: So Max von Pettenkoffer was the last great defender of miasmas.
sentences.zh: 马克斯·冯·佩滕科弗是瘴气论最后一位伟大的捍卫者。

sentences.en: He was born in 1818 and he died in 1901.
sentences.zh: 他出生于1818年，卒于1901年。

sentences.en: And pretty much to the end, he was arguing and fighting passionately for miasmas
sentences.zh: 直到最后，他几乎都在为瘴气是霍乱、伤寒等疾病的病因，

sentences.en: as being the cause of diseases like cholera and typhoid and on and on and on.
sentences.zh: 而进行着充满激情的辩论和抗争。

sentences.en: In his day, he was not considered a crank.
sentences.zh: 在他那个时代，他并不被视为怪人。

sentences.en: In fact, just the opposite.
sentences.zh: 事实上，恰恰相反。

sentences.en: He was revered.
sentences.zh: 他备受尊崇。

sentences.en: He was considered the world expert on cholera.
sentences.zh: 他被认为是世界级的霍乱专家。

sentences.en: And so what were van Pettenkoffer's ideas about cholera?
sentences.zh: 那么，冯·佩滕科弗关于霍乱的观点是什么？

sentences.en: Cholera comes to Europe in the 19th century in this series of epidemics that are totally terrifying.
sentences.zh: 19世纪，霍乱传入欧洲，引发了一系列极其恐怖的流行病。

sentences.en: A city would be running along smoothly and everything seemed fine one day.
sentences.zh: 一座城市可能前一天还运行平稳，一切看起来都很正常。

sentences.en: And the next day, people are just dropping dead in the street.
sentences.zh: 但第二天，人们就纷纷倒毙在街头。

sentences.en: Their faces are turning blue.
sentences.zh: 他们的脸变成了蓝色。

sentences.en: They are suffering violent cramps and diarrhea.
sentences.zh: 他们遭受着剧烈的痉挛和腹泻。

sentences.en: And within a few days, they're dead.
sentences.zh: 几天之内，他们就死了。

sentences.en: You know, thousands and thousands and thousands of people are dying in city after city after city.
sentences.zh: 你知道，成千上万的人在城市接连不断地死去。

sentences.en: So what is it?
sentences.zh: 那么，这到底是什么？

sentences.en: So van Pettenkoffer believed that cholera was actually caused by fumes that came out of the ground.
sentences.zh: 冯·佩滕科弗认为，霍乱实际上是由从地下冒出的气体引起的。

sentences.en: That there were the certain kinds of bacteria that could ferment, basically,
sentences.zh: 他认为某些细菌可以在潮湿且条件适宜的土壤中发酵，

sentences.en: in soil that was damp and just had just the right conditions.
sentences.zh: 基本上就是这样。

sentences.en: So you would have these fumes that they would release and they would build up inside of buildings,
sentences.zh: 所以，这些细菌会释放出气体，并在建筑物内积聚，

sentences.en: inside of people's homes, especially if they were poorly ventilated.
sentences.zh: 特别是在通风不良的家庭住宅中。

sentences.en: So people would, you know, be breathing this stuff in and out, in and out.
sentences.zh: 人们会不断地吸入和呼出这些东西。

sentences.en: And it would create damage inside their bodies that would eventually
sentences.zh: 这会在他们体内造成损害，最终

sentences.en: trigger all the horrible, deadly symptoms of cholera.
sentences.zh: 引发霍乱所有可怕的致命症状。

sentences.en: And so he was very concerned to keep the air safe.
sentences.zh: 因此，他非常关心如何保持空气安全。

sentences.en: So what were his ideas about how to do that, about how to keep the air safe?
sentences.zh: 那么，他对于如何做到这一点，如何保持空气安全，有什么想法？

sentences.en: Well, he believed that you have to prevent these fumes from reaching people.
sentences.zh: 嗯，他认为你必须防止这些气体接触到人。

sentences.en: So one way you can do that is to try to avoid the circumstances in which these fumes can form.
sentences.zh: 所以，一种方法是尽量避免这些气体形成的条件。

sentences.en: You can build buildings on soil that he believed was safer, for example.
sentences.zh: 例如，你可以把建筑物建在他认为更安全的土壤上。

sentences.en: He made lots of changes in Munich to the water system so that you wouldn't have a lot of stagnant
sentences.zh: 他在慕尼黑对供水系统做了很多改变，这样就不会有大量的死水

sentences.en: water sitting around, which he believed that would be a problem.
sentences.zh: 积存，他认为那会是个问题。

sentences.en: He emphasizes ventilation.
sentences.zh: 他强调通风。

sentences.en: You want to get fresh air moving through your house or your office or your school,
sentences.zh: 你想让新鲜空气在你的房子、办公室或学校里流通，

sentences.en: because if there's no way for air to get out, these fumes that he imagined were rising up from
sentences.zh: 因为如果空气无法排出，他所想象的从地下升起的气体，

sentences.en: the ground are just going to get into these rooms and get trapped in there.
sentences.zh: 就会进入这些房间并被困在里面。

sentences.en: And then you just breathe him and breathe him and breathe him.
sentences.zh: 然后你就会不断地吸入它。

sentences.en: And he was part of a movement.
sentences.zh: 他是一场运动的一部分。

sentences.en: You know, they called themselves sanitarians and they wanted to help everyone.
sentences.zh: 你知道，他们自称为“卫生学家”，他们想帮助所有人。

sentences.en: And so, you know, tenements in New York or hospitals for the poor in London or what have you,
sentences.zh: 所以，你知道，纽约的廉租房，或者伦敦的贫民医院等等，

sentences.en: they were all trying to get fresh air to people.
sentences.zh: 他们都在努力为人们提供新鲜空气。

sentences.en: They were all trying to fight miasmas and thereby fight disease.
sentences.zh: 他们都在努力对抗瘴气，从而对抗疾病。

sentences.en: I mean, you wrote that the New York City Board of Health forced the installation of 46,000 new windows
sentences.zh: 我的意思是，你写道，纽约市卫生委员会强制在全市安装了46000扇新窗户，

sentences.en: throughout the city, which sounds, I mean, that's an intense buy-in.
sentences.zh: 这听起来，我的意思是，这是一种强烈的投入。

sentences.en: I mean, that's a very expensive proposition.
sentences.zh: 我的意思是，这是一个非常昂贵的提议。

sentences.en: Yeah, absolutely.
sentences.zh: 是的，绝对是。

sentences.en: Absolutely.
sentences.zh: 绝对是。

sentences.en: I mean, you know, New York was much smaller of a city at the time.
sentences.zh: 我的意思是，你知道，当时的纽约还是个小得多的城市。

sentences.en: So that is just huge.
sentences.zh: 所以这规模非常巨大。

sentences.en: Yeah.
sentences.zh: 是的。

sentences.en: These sanitarians and these reformers were able to get a lot of things pushed through.
sentences.zh: 这些卫生学家和改革者能够推动很多事情的落实。

sentences.en: And, you know, Florence Nightingale was very much part of this movement as well.
sentences.zh: 而且，你知道，弗洛伦斯·南丁格尔也是这场运动的重要参与者。

sentences.en: And she designed new kinds of hospitals with long corridors and rooms branching off of them,
sentences.zh: 她设计了新型医院，有长长的走廊和从走廊延伸出去的房间，

sentences.en: all designed to maximize the flow of air, to get fresh air into for these patients,
sentences.zh: 所有设计都是为了最大限度地增加空气流通，为病人引入新鲜空气，

sentences.en: because she was convinced that they were getting sick, not from contagious disease, but from miasmas.
sentences.zh: 因为她确信他们生病不是因为传染病，而是因为瘴气。

sentences.en: So as popular as the miasma theory was, the idea that bad vibes or animal carcasses or stagnant
sentences.zh: 所以，尽管瘴气理论很流行，但认为坏情绪、动物尸体或死水

sentences.en: water was corrupting the air with poisonous fumes was obviously wrong.
sentences.zh: 正在用有毒气体腐蚀空气的想法显然是错误的。

sentences.en: And over time, you get this competing philosophy, which is germ theory, which we now know is correct.
sentences.zh: 随着时间的推移，出现了一种相互竞争的哲学，即细菌理论，我们现在知道它是正确的。

sentences.en: Can you talk about how germ theorists started to win the battle of ideas against sanitarians
sentences.zh: 你能谈谈细菌理论家是如何开始在思想之战中战胜像冯·佩滕科弗这样的卫生学家的吗？

sentences.en: like von Pettenkoffer?
sentences.zh: 你知道，在17世纪，人们开始发明显微镜。

sentences.en: You know, in the 1600s, people are starting to invent microscopes.
sentences.zh: 当他们通过显微镜观察时，突然发现有各种各样的

sentences.en: And when they look through the microscopes, they suddenly discover there are all these
sentences.zh: 微小生物，是我们以前不知道的。

sentences.en: tiny creatures that we didn't know about before.
sentences.zh: 他们称之为细菌、微生物，或者，你知道，细菌。

sentences.en: They would call them germs or microbes or, you know, bacteria.
sentences.zh: 就像他们对这些东西有各种各样的称呼一样。

sentences.en: Like they had all sorts of names for these things.
sentences.zh: 早在18世纪初，就有人说，你知道，这些细菌是瘟疫、肺结核等疾病的病因，

sentences.en: And as early as the early 1700s, you had people saying, you know, these germs are the cause
sentences.zh: 不一而足。

sentences.en: of diseases like plague and tuberculosis and on and on and on and on.
sentences.zh: 他们被称为“传染病论者”。

sentences.en: And they got to be known as the contagionists.
sentences.zh: 每个人都认为他们疯了。

sentences.en: And everyone thought they were crazy.
sentences.zh: 但在19世纪，证据慢慢积累起来，证明，是的，实际上，

sentences.en: But slowly in the 19th century, the evidence started to accrue that, yeah, actually,
